implementation_notes: In Rails the query object is ActiveRecord::Relation: scope methods (where, joins, order, limit, group, having, includes) each return a new relation instead of executing, and and/or combine two relations into the logical intersection or union, requiring them to be structurally compatible (same model, differing only by where or having); SQL is rendered when the relation is enumerated. What replaces the classic query class is the relation plus Arel beneath it; find_by_sql and sanitize_sql stay justified for statements the relation API cannot express.
code_sketch:
rel = Customer.where(status: 'active')
rel = rel.where('age >= ?', min_age) if min_age
rel = rel.order(:name).limit(50)
rel.and(Customer.where(country: 'DE')).each { |c| puts c.name }
pitfalls: and/or raise on structurally incompatible relations: same model and same where/having shape only - mixing joins or order between the operands breaks them.
Interpolating values into where("... #{v}") disables binding; keep the placeholder form where('age >= ?', v).
Relations cache their loaded rows: reusing a loaded relation returns stale data, and holding one across requests can pin a connection.
